Hi Mark. Last class you sorted out the three futures. Today we work on a structure that has nothing to do with meaning and everything to do with weight. It is called inversion, and English uses it when a negative or limiting expression is moved to the front of the sentence. Here is the mechanism. Normally you say, the studio has rarely taken a risk like this. If you move rarely to the front, the sentence must switch to question order. Rarely has the studio taken a risk like this. Same meaning, much more weight. The trigger words are the ones to memorise. Never, rarely, seldom, hardly ever, not only, no sooner, under no circumstances, only when, only after, and little, as in little did we know. Two things go wrong for Brazilian students. The first is forgetting the auxiliary. If the verb has no auxiliary of its own, you borrow do, does or did. Not only does it look extraordinary. The second is inverting the wrong clause after only when. There the flip lands on the main clause, not the first one. Only when you reach the third act does the structure make sense. Keep it rare. One inversion in a paragraph is powerful, and three in a row sound like a robot. Before class, find a review in English and look for one. See you on Friday, Mark.

Right, the verdict, and I have thought about this for a week. Not only does this game look extraordinary, but it also runs perfectly on hardware that should not be able to handle it, which almost nobody talks about. Rarely have I seen a studio this careful with something so large. The world is immersive in the way people always claim and almost never deliver: you can stand in one place for a minute and the city keeps working around you. Now the shortcomings, because there are two. The story falls short in the middle. Around the twelve hour mark you get four missions that exist only to slow you down, and they are the most underwhelming hours in the whole thing. And the map is overrated by everybody reviewing it, because size is not the same as density. Only when you reach the third act does the writing finally live up to the world it is set in. So, a recommendation with one condition. Under no circumstances should you play this in short sessions. Give it two hours at a time or do not start it at all. It is not flawless, and it is the best thing this studio has ever made.

First, you state the verdict in one sentence, so the reader knows where you stand before anything else. Then you give the strongest praise, and that is where an inversion earns its place, because the sentence carries the most weight in the whole review. After that, you name the shortcomings honestly, in plain word order, because a criticism does not need extra weight to be heard. Next, you add the condition, the thing the reader has to do for the recommendation to hold. Finally, you close with a balanced line that admits the flaw and keeps the recommendation standing.
